# Parsing floats

Reading decimal text into the nearest float32, float64 or wide float, exactly.

<h2 id="retained-decimal-digits"><code>RetainedDecimalDigits</code></h2>

```rux
pub const RetainedDecimalDigits: uint = 768;
```

How many significant digits a narrow float reader keeps before the rest becomes a sticky bit.
Seven hundred and sixty-eight, which is the longest exact decimal expansion any midpoint between two adjacent
`float64` values has. Keeping that many means a tie is detected exactly, and a nonzero digit beyond them means
the value cannot be a tie at all — so the bound is where the two arguments meet rather than a round number.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/NarrowParse.rux#L24)

<h2 id="exact-float64"><code>ExactFloat64</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ExactFloat64(digits: &FixedNat, exponent: int, truncated: bool, negative: bool, value: *var float64, overflowed: *var bool) -> bool
```

Reads the decimal `digits * 10^exponent` into the nearest `float64`, with ties to even.
Answers false for a value past the format's range or a workspace failure, with `overflowed` saying which.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/NarrowParse.rux#L276)

**Parameters**

| Name         | Type           | Description                                                 |
| ------------ | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `digits`     | `&FixedNat`    | the retained significant digits                             |
| `exponent`   | `int`          | the power of ten they are scaled by                         |
| `truncated`  | `bool`         | whether a nonzero digit was dropped past the retained bound |
| `negative`   | `bool`         | whether the value is negative                               |
| `value`      | `*var float64` | receives the float                                          |
| `overflowed` | `*var bool`    | receives whether the failure was the value being too large  |

**Returns**: true when the value was read

<h2 id="exact-float32"><code>ExactFloat32</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ExactFloat32(digits: &FixedNat, exponent: int, truncated: bool, negative: bool, value: *var float32, overflowed: *var bool) -> bool
```

Reads the decimal `digits * 10^exponent` into the nearest `float32`, with ties to even.
Read at this width's own precision rather than at a `float64`'s and narrowed: narrowing rounds a second time,
and a value that lands on a `float32` boundary can round the wrong way when it has already been rounded to
fifty-three bits on the way.
Answers false for a value past the format's range or a workspace failure, with `overflowed` saying which.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/NarrowParse.rux#L300)

**Parameters**

| Name         | Type           | Description                                                 |
| ------------ | -------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `digits`     | `&FixedNat`    | the retained significant digits                             |
| `exponent`   | `int`          | the power of ten they are scaled by                         |
| `truncated`  | `bool`         | whether a nonzero digit was dropped past the retained bound |
| `negative`   | `bool`         | whether the value is negative                               |
| `value`      | `*var float32` | receives the float                                          |
| `overflowed` | `*var bool`    | receives whether the failure was the value being too large  |

**Returns**: true when the value was read

<h2 id="decimal-reading"><code>DecimalReading</code></h2>

```rux
pub struct DecimalReading {
    pub digits: FixedNat;
    pub exponent: int;
    pub significant: uint;
    pub truncated: bool;
    pub negative: bool;
    pub special: int;
}
```

What a decimal spells, before any format decides what to do with it.
Copy, holding the retained digits and the two flags the rounding needs.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/ParseFloat64.rux#L55)

**Fields**

| Name          | Type       | Description                                                                                            |
| ------------- | ---------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `digits`      | `FixedNat` | The retained significant digits, as an integer.                                                        |
| `exponent`    | `int`      | The power of ten they are scaled by, counting the decimal point and any digits dropped past the bound. |
| `significant` | `uint`     | How many significant digits were retained.                                                             |
| `truncated`   | `bool`     | Whether a nonzero digit was dropped past the retained bound.                                           |
| `negative`    | `bool`     | Whether the value is negative, including a negative zero.                                              |
| `special`     | `int`      | Zero for an ordinary number, one for `NaN`, two for an infinity.                                       |

<h2 id="scan-decimal"><code>ScanDecimal</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ScanDecimal(str: char8[..], reading: *var DecimalReading) -> ! ParseError
```

Reads the decimal grammar out of `str`, without deciding what float it names.
One scanner for both narrow widths, so what one reads the other reads: the grammar is
`[+-]?(digits[.digits?]?|.digits)([eE][+-]?digits)?`, plus the two special spellings `NaN` and `Inf` exactly as
formatting writes them. The digits are kept exactly up to [`RetainedDecimalDigits`](/docs/api/format/parse-float#retained-decimal-digits), past which a nonzero one
sets `truncated` and moves the exponent instead.
Reports `Empty` for no bytes, `InvalidCharacter` at the byte where the shape stopped matching, and
`OutOfMemory` where the retained digits would not fit the workspace.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/ParseFloat64.rux#L81)

**Parameters**

| Name      | Type                  | Description                      |
| --------- | --------------------- | -------------------------------- |
| `str`     | `char8[..]`           | the text to read                 |
| `reading` | `*var DecimalReading` | receives what the decimal spells |

**Returns**: success when the whole text was the grammar

<h2 id="parse-float64"><code>ParseFloat64</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ParseFloat64(str: char8[..]) -> float64 ! ParseError
pub func ParseFloat64(str: StringView) -> float64 ! ParseError
```

Reads `str` as the `float64` nearest what it spells, rounding to nearest with ties to even.
Exact: the value is formed as a ratio of integers and the quotient is taken with a sticky bit, so what comes
back is the nearest `float64` and never one step off it. `NaN`, `Inf` and `-Inf` are read exactly as formatting
writes them.
Reports `Empty`, `InvalidCharacter` and `OutOfMemory` as [`ScanDecimal`](/docs/api/format/parse-float#scan-decimal) does, and `Overflow` at the text's
length for a value past the largest finite `float64` — refused rather than rounded to an infinity, since that
would turn a number the caller wrote into one they did not. A value below the smallest subnormal is the signed
zero it rounds to.

| Overload                                                         | Summary                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func ParseFloat64(str: char8[..]) -> float64 ! ParseError`  | Reads `str` as the `float64` nearest what it spells, rounding to nearest with ties to even. |
| `pub func ParseFloat64(str: StringView) -> float64 ! ParseError` | Provides the public `ParseFloat64` operation.                                               |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/ParseFloat64.rux#L191)

**Parameters**

| Name  | Type                       | Description      |
| ----- | -------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `str` | `char8[..]` / `StringView` | the text to read |

**Returns**: the value, or why the text is not one

<h2 id="parse-float32"><code>ParseFloat32</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ParseFloat32(str: char8[..]) -> float32 ! ParseError
pub func ParseFloat32(str: StringView) -> float32 ! ParseError
```

Reads `str` as the `float32` nearest what it spells, rounding to nearest with ties to even.
Read at this width's own precision rather than at a `float64`'s and narrowed. Narrowing rounds a second time,
and a value that lands on a `float32` boundary can round the wrong way once it has already been rounded to
fifty-three bits on the way there.
The failures [`ParseFloat64`](/docs/api/format/parse-float#parse-float64) reports, at this width's range: `Overflow` for a value past the largest finite
`float32`, and the signed zero for one below the smallest subnormal.

| Overload                                                         | Summary                                                                                     |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `pub func ParseFloat32(str: char8[..]) -> float32 ! ParseError`  | Reads `str` as the `float32` nearest what it spells, rounding to nearest with ties to even. |
| `pub func ParseFloat32(str: StringView) -> float32 ! ParseError` | The same grammar for a view.                                                                |

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/ParseFloat64.rux#L245)

**Parameters**

| Name  | Type                       | Description      |
| ----- | -------------------------- | ---------------- |
| `str` | `char8[..]` / `StringView` | the text to read |

**Returns**: the value, or why the text is not one

<h2 id="parse-wide-float"><code>ParseWideFloat</code></h2>

```rux
pub func ParseWideFloat(allocator: Allocator, str: char8[..], layout: &FloatLayout) -> uint512 ! ParseError
```

Reads `str` as a value under `layout`, rounding to nearest with ties to even, and reports the bits.
Overflow is refused rather than rounded to infinity, as [`ParseFloat64`](/docs/api/format/parse-float#parse-float64) refuses it; a value too small for the
format becomes the signed zero. `NaN`, `Inf` and `-Inf` are read exactly as formatting writes them.

[Source](https://github.com/rux-lang/Rux/blob/main/Packages/Format/Src/WideFloatParse.rux#L18)

**Parameters**

| Name        | Type           | Description                                      |
| ----------- | -------------- | ------------------------------------------------ |
| `allocator` | `Allocator`    | where the working storage comes from             |
| `str`       | `char8[..]`    | the text to parse                                |
| `layout`    | `&FloatLayout` | which wide floating-point format the bits are in |

**Returns**: the bit pattern, or the failure and where it was found
